    {
     "subtitle": "Good evening, the win over Dinamo and congratulations to the whole Hajduk fan family",
     "screenshot_description": "Presenter Frane greets viewers in the studio, while presenter Vinko sits beside him with a microphone in front of him. The screen shows the show title HŽV Siempre and the headline VELIČANSTVENA POBJEDA HAJDUKA.",
     "content": "The show opens with a playful greeting: presenter **Frane** welcomes „the good people and those a little less good“, and then, together with Vinko, opens the conversation about the match that ended with Hajduk’s victory over Dinamo at Poljud. Frane immediately extends congratulations to the whole Hajduk fan family and the team, stressing that the win came in a dramatic finish and that after so many years of waiting, the fans had to celebrate.\n\nPresenter **Vinko** builds on the introduction and points out that Saturday was rainy, but that the atmosphere after the match cannot be gloomy. Frane admits that the presenters, as he puts it, could hardly wait for the end so they could talk live and share their impressions. In doing so, he returns to the show’s usual topic: fan reactions and conversation with viewers who get in touch through messages.\n\nVinko cites a comment from one viewer who, before the derby, predicted that the game would be played in mud and that Hajduk did not have Ivan Gudelj. Vinko points out that in the end his team looked like „one Ivan Gudelj“, meaning that the whole squad showed the same commitment and fighting spirit that their teammate normally brought to the defense. Such an impression, he says, was his first thought after the match.",

     "subtitle": "A rainy Saturday, dripping from the structure and fans divided across the stands",
     "screenshot_description": "View of the Poljud stands during the rain, with wet seats visible and fans spreading out across the stands.",
     "content": "Frane then reflects on the weather conditions and describes the paradox of the rainy Saturday, when, as he puts it, the sun was shining „outside“ and everyone was in good spirits. He adds that it rained almost the whole day and was so heavy that it seemed it would never stop. Vinko comments on the forecasts and points out that the fans had expected a game in mud, and that this is exactly what happened.\n\nGuest **1** in the studio follows up on the topic of the weather and ironically mentions a mobile app that showed a one hundred percent chance of rain, while in the end the downpour came exactly when it was supposed to. At the same time, Frane explains that a panel on one part of the stadium was particularly annoying, because water dripped directly onto the fans, specifically on the east side.\n\nFrane also describes how the fans spread out. The east side was under water and dripping, so many moved to the west side, which was cleaner and had more space. In the end, as Frane points out, part of the crowd retreated toward the upper rows and passageways, while the worst off were those in the north, because there was nowhere for them to escape.",

     "subtitle": "The fight for every ball: how the conditions shaped the rhythm of the game",
     "screenshot_description": "Hajduk players in a duel on the wet pitch, with the ball sliding across the water in the penalty area.",
     "content": "The conversation then moves to the course of the game itself. Frane points out that the team played with a lot of fight and that after every lost ball, they immediately tried to win back possession. He stresses that this is exactly what has been demanded of Hajduk for years: a fight for every ball and every duel. Frane concludes that this mental strength was key to the result.\n\nVinko agrees and adds that the conditions on the pitch were extremely demanding. The pitch was waterlogged and slippery, so the game often resembled water polo rather than football. That is precisely why, Vinko says, it was no wonder that short and clumsy moves, stops and sudden clearances of the ball kept appearing.\n\nFrane notes that such conditions cannot be fully controlled, but that the game can be adapted. He says the team showed this and that, in that context, the mistakes were understandable. Vinko follows up and points out that it is important the team maintained its concentration until the end.",

     "content": "Vinko presents an analysis according to which Hajduk controlled the game for most of the match. He says that Dinamo did not show it could do anything significant without Hajduk’s help, meaning that Hajduk’s own errors created space for the opponent. He emphasizes that the key was that Hajduk’s players were half a step faster and were always in the right place.\n\nFrane agrees and adds that Hajduk had more chances and more mature opportunities. He says the actions were of better quality, and when everything is considered, there is no doubt who dominated the match. He also recalls a moment when one error almost opened the way for the opponent, but Hajduk ultimately controlled the rhythm.\n\nVinko concludes that his impression is key: Dinamo did not look like a team that could turn the course of the derby around. He adds that Hajduk should then use its advantage in the next matches too, because this type of play proved effective.",

He adds that even in the case of one yellow card at the start of the match, which was almost instant, the referee showed inconsistency.\n\nIn this part of the conversation, Frane compares the decisions with other matches. He recalls the case of Brajković and says that one yellow card in Osijek had different consequences than the cards at Poljud. Frane concludes that such things keep repeating and that referee consistency remains an open question. He also sarcastically comments on an alleged history of refereeing in favor of one club, but this part was expressed as his opinion, not as an established fact.",

Frane joins in the congratulations and himself thanks him for it. The congratulations extend to various other viewers as well, and Frane wishes a happy birthday to one of the viewers and talks about the feeling of satisfaction at having received such messages after the match.\n\nAlong with this, messages from Sisak and other places are mentioned, so Frane sends greetings to the people of Sisak, as well as to individual fans who were at the stadium. Part of the conversation is also devoted to the group that followed the match from the stands, and Frane also mentions the Torcida choreography as one of the most beautiful moments of the day.",

He believes one ball that was cleared into the middle was decisive and that such situations must be corrected in the next matches. Frane agrees that the defensive organization was problematic, but stresses that the team ultimately managed to keep the lead.\n\nVinko notes that the goalkeeper showed good reactions on several shots, but that at one point his coming off his line was not decisive enough. He concludes that the mistakes were concentrated in a few minutes, so it is important for the team to focus on how to avoid them in the future.",

Guest **1** adds that the defense looked insecure in several places and that it would be good if the players reduced such mistakes. As an example, he cites situations in which awkward ball clearances occurred.\n\nVinko concludes that after such a match it is important to assess players correctly, without excessive euphoria, but also without ignoring problems.      "content": "After the analysis of the full-backs and the midfield, presenter **Frane** moves on to the defensive line and the rating of the center-backs.      "content": "The conversation in this part of the show moves from general impressions to individual player ratings. Presenter **Frane** points out that **Bamba** on the right wing was one of Hajduk’s most important players in the derby. In his view, Bamba opened space with his movement and created problems for Dinamo’s defense, and on several occasions he also entered the final phase of the attack himself. Frane concludes that he is a player who was the best in the team, and that his performance was ‘key’ for the middle of the pitch and for the width of the attack.\n\nPresenter **Vinko** stresses that Bamba was not only an attacker, but also a player who worked in defense and came to balls in his own half. Although he considers him an important factor, Vinko warns that his game also had moments of insecurity, such as bad passes and imprecise decisions in the final stage. Still, he concludes that the positive aspects were more dominant.\n\nThe conversation also mentions that in the second half Bamba was under great physical strain because of the slippery pitch, which further hindered his work. Frane recalls that, despite this, Bamba remained active in the fight for every ball, which, according to him, was one of the characteristics of the whole team that evening.",

     "content": "In this part, the conversation focuses on specific attacking situations. **Frane** recalls that Hajduk had more chances and more mature opportunities than Dinamo in the derby, but that some of these chances were wasted because of imprecise finishing. He especially mentions that **Bamba** had several situations in which he should have scored, yet he missed them. Vinko praised that move as an example of good cooperation on the wing and in midfield, and Frane added that Bamba had ‘made up for’ his mistakes with it. He also mentions that Bamba was in several situations where he was offside, which further reduced his impact in the final stage.\n\nThis segment points to a paradox of the attacking play: Hajduk created enough chances, but their conversion remained uneven, which, despite the win, left room for criticism.",

     "subtitle": "Coaching psychology: how the reaction to a goal became a topic",
     "screenshot_description": "The coach in the technical area after a goal, with a visible emotional reaction, while his behavior is discussed in the studio.",
     "content": "In this part, the conversation moves from the game to the psychology of the coach. **Frane** believes the coach’s reaction to the goal was ‘key’ for the whole atmosphere on the bench and in the stands. According to him, at the moment of the goal the coach showed an emotion that reflected how much the match meant to him, and that, in Frane’s view, is part of what is called coaching psychology.\n\n**Vinko** agrees that the reaction was visible and showed how personal the win is for the coach. He stresses that the coach’s joy at that moment was ‘natural’ and mirrored the months-long pressure that surrounded the club. He adds that such a reaction is often more important than tactical moves, because it transfers energy to the players.\n\nThe conversation also touches on the criticism previously directed at the coach. Vinko states that in this situation he ‘will no longer mock him’, but that one should accept the coach’s flaws while also acknowledging his contribution to the match. Frane stresses that the coach’s influence is not measured only through substitutions, but also through the way he supports the team in critical moments.\n\nThis topic opens a wider debate about how much emotions and motivation in football are linked to the result and to public perception.",

     "content": "In this segment, the conversation focuses on the strikers **Livaja** and **Šego**. **Frane** is critical of Livaja’s play in the recent matches, stating that he missed situations that should have ‘lifted’ him. As an example, he cites situations in which Šego was in good positions but failed to convert the chance.\n\n**Vinko**, on the other hand, softens the criticism. He reminds us that Šego has advantages that Livaja does not have, and vice versa, and that these are two different striker profiles. In his view, Hajduk needs both players, but it seems the coach is not using them in the right way. This also raises the question of why Livaja stayed out of the game for so long, despite the fact that at some moments a real striker was needed.\n\n**Guest 1** adds that in the final minutes Šego stayed on the pitch longer than necessary, while Livaja remained out of the game, which further prompted debate about the real role of strikers in the final stage of the match.",

     "subtitle": "Substitutions and Šutalo on the right wing: the question of coaching vision",
     "screenshot_description": "Šutalo on the pitch at the moment of his entry, with his position on the right wing and the substitution board showing the changes.",
     "content": "One of the key segments concerns the substitutions. **Frane** states that the first substitution was **Šutalo**, who came on on the right side, but that the coach later insisted that he play on the left side. Frane believes Šutalo on the right wing would be a better solution, because he is fast, defensively solid and capable of short runs.\n\nAccording to Frane’s words, the coach did not show a clear intention as to why Šutalo should not stay on the right wing. Instead, a ‘double substitution’ occurred, in which players were moved from one side to the other, which disrupted the team’s rhythm.
